title: Feelings Wheel
description: An interactive wheel following the psychological feelings wheel developed by Dr. Gloria Wilcox in an attempt to reduce phone usage in existing greenspaces and encourage individuals to connect with themselves and their feelings while also facilitating conversation with those around them!
overlayHTML:
Feelings Wheel



Oct 2024-Nov 2025

This was a project where we were challenged to create an intervention for a third space. My group chose parks as our third place, conducting various forms of research in order to determine what we would like to make. I conducted photo studies of Central Park and Prospect Park as well as research on interventions conducted in existing green spaces.


Project as Site: Socialization

Once we consolidated this research, we decided on an intervention that prioritized mental health to get people off of their phones and encourage them to not only look inwards but engage with others and connect with them! We used the feelings wheel developed by Dr. Gloria Wilcox to develop an interactive display that encouraged users to spin a wheel representing how they feel! The initial plan was to have the other divisions of the wheel within each "pie slice", however this was unfeasible due to the tight timeline, we ended up having them separate. We wanted to encourage people in the park to come up to the display using the bright colors and the mirror on which they could take selfies. On the back, people could write their reflections with a whiteboard marker and engage with others as they added their contributions to the back panel. I was in charge of the design and fabrication of this interactive display. I chose the clear acrylic for the panels to encourage transparency and show all the participants the separate denominations of the emotions.

I originally designed it in AutoDesk Fusion to see how all the separate parts worked together. Then I laser cut a mini-prototype before assembling and painting the final version. Something I didn't account for was the lack of support for the heavy panels beyond the spinning circle and the floor panel. I ended up using the scraps from my laser cut pieces, like the cut out circles to create a bubble like effect connecting the front and back panels together!



City as Site

Another thing I added was a breathing exercise toy in the case that there would be a line so that participants had something to do while waiting. The breathing exercise takes the box breathing method and guides the user through it using a rectangle a movable "button" that slides through a slot to guide the exercise. It was another attempt to get the user to get in touch with themselves and help them potentially destress!

title: Phone Stand
description: A phone stand for documentation to be placed on top of a desk or surface. It can be adjusted for the size of the phone as well
overlayHTML:
Document Camera Mount


when phone filming vertically
when phone filming horizontally


Sept 2024- Oct 2024


The task: Build a mount that can hold your phone or another camera above your workspace. As someone who wanted to get into content creation, especially through filming my art process. I struggled with this a lot at home because my desk had two tiers, a short shelf on top and the desk below. It was difficult to place my phone at an optimal distance past the shelf to capture my desk, especially when I would make stop motion animations, for which the stillness of the camera is crucial. Depending on the format however, I knew that my phone may need to be horizontal and vertical. In addition, this needed to fit a variety of phones in case I got a bigger or smaller phone. In addition, depending on the desk, there would need to be different options for how far the platform should reach. After prototyping the device in cardboard I realized that the weight of the phone would eventually be too much for the device to handle on its own. But serendipitously, I also realized I tended to either watch TV or look at my reference pictures while working, so I extended the back of the device to hold the weight of the iPad to counter the weight of the phone. I modeled it in Autodesk Fusion first to see how all the slots fit together and determine the spacing before converting them to DXF files to composit in Illustrator.
